bolivar-dr--cofradia.description: Bolívar Cofradía dates from the late 1990s and is made in Honduras from aged Honduran and Nicaraguan long filler and a Connecticut Broadleaf binder under an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Bold and full-bodied, it smokes earthy and peppery with coffee, roasted nuts and a little chocolate.

thirds.notes: Molasses sweetness, black coffee, earth and cedar, with roasted nuts and a light pepper.
Coffee grows with black pepper; the smoke turns nuttier and creamier and the wood shifts toward oak.
Coffee and nuts return with buttery notes, and the heat builds to an earthy, peppery finish.

sources.title: JR Cigar – Re-discover the Bolívar Cofradía

bolivar-dr--cofradia-oscuro.description: Released in 2024 and rolled at HATSA in Honduras, Cofradía Oscuro sets an aged Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and Dominican, Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. A little above medium in strength, it pairs earth and black pepper with dark chocolate, black coffee and leather, and a light citrus-peel sweetness.

thirds.notes: Bold earth and pepper with a quiet sweetness, citrus peel and light apple, the coffee turning toward dark chocolate.
Dark chocolate and black coffee with a leathery, peppery finish, while the sweetness starts to fade.
Mostly earthy, the black pepper intensifying, with leather, coffee and a touch of brown sugar.

sources.title: Cigar Czars – Bolívar Cofradía Oscuro review
Tiny Tim's Blog – Bolívar Cofradía Oscuro Robusto

bolivar-dr--aniversario.description: A 2026 limited edition marking more than 130 years of the Bolívar name, Aniversario is rolled at HATSA in Danlí, Honduras, from South American tobacco: an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, a Brazilian Arapiraca binder and filler from Brazil, Argentina, Colombia and Paraguay. Medium to full, it combines cedar and pepper with buttery earth, leather and baking spice.

thirds.notes: Pepper and buttery earth with a soft sweetness and spice, settling into cedar, stone fruit and leather.
Cedar leads as the pepper softens into warm baking spice and the Brazilian binder's earthiness comes forward.
A grain-like sweetness shapes the finish, over earth, cedar and lingering spice.

sources.title: Stogie Press – Bolívar Aniversario Toro review

bolivar-dr--heritage.description: Bolívar Heritage, made in the Dominican Republic, wraps a dark, silky Connecticut Habano leaf around an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and long filler from Nicaragua, Honduras, Mexico and the Dominican Republic. Medium and milder than other Bolívars, it holds a steady line of earth, leather, cedar and spice from start to finish.
